Thought: To determine the point group, I need to understand the molecular structure of CS(=O)C (dimethyl sulfoxide). Let me visualize this molecule and analyze its symmetry elements.

The SMILES notation CS(=O)C represents:
- A central sulfur atom (S)
- Two methyl groups (C) attached to the sulfur
- One oxygen atom (=O) double-bonded to the sulfur

This gives a tetrahedral-like arrangement around the sulfur, but with different substituents (2 methyl groups, 1 oxygen, and 1 lone pair). The molecule has:
- No proper rotation axis (C₂, C₃, etc.)
- A mirror plane that contains the S=O bond and bisects the C-S-C angle
- No inversion center
- No improper rotation axes

The presence of only a mirror plane (σ) as a symmetry element indicates that this molecule belongs to the Cs point group.
